strengths: The motivation is convincing: Section 2 provides an explicit confounded SCM where ignoring context or intervening on every controllable variable prevents attaining the optimum and causes linear regret.

Combining POMPS reduction, contextual BO within each scope, and an averaged-UCB scope selector offers a useful modular approach. The multi-function BO formulation is potentially relevant beyond causal optimisation.

Experiments use 110 seeds, 700 interventions, and uncertainty intervals, with additional noise, optimiser-backend, and context ablations. The examples demonstrate meaningful benefits from contextual information and dimensionality reduction.
weaknesses: The reduction from general mixed policies to the analysed bandit model is insufficiently justified. Definition 1 permits sequential scopes such as {(A; empty), (B; C)} when A affects C: the agent must intervene on A before observing C. Algorithm 2 instead samples all contexts from a fixed distribution before choosing actions. Grouping scopes only by their aggregate intervention and context sets also requires justification because individual policies have different information restrictions. Additional causal restrictions or a sequential formulation are needed.

The regret proof contains substantive gaps. On page 27, Appendix B.2 bounds action regret by the variation of the optimal reward across contexts; that variation can be zero while action regret is positive. Moreover, the instance-dependent derivation ends with the worst-arm information gain through c(T), whereas Equation (4) claims the potentially smaller averaged information gain. These discrepancies require a corrected proof before the stated guarantees can be accepted.

The theoretical algorithm and experimental implementation are not clearly connected. The analysis assumes independent GPs with known kernels, fixed Gaussian observation noise, and compact domains, while HEBO learns transformations and hyperparameters and several experimental SCMs fall outside these assumptions. The manuscript should distinguish guarantees for idealised UCB-BO from empirical behaviour of the implemented method.

Evaluation covers a small collection of constructed SCMs, generally with only one or two POMPSs. Several comparisons deliberately prevent the baseline from attaining the optimum. Functional Causal BO is discussed but not evaluated, and there is no comparison of the proposed scope selector against uniform selection or alternative bandit selectors using identical scopes and BO backends. Consequently, the incremental benefit of the new selection mechanism remains unclear.

The scalability claim is not adequately supported. Section 3 explicitly requires exponential scope enumeration, but reports no preprocessing timings, memory measurements, or scaling with the number of candidate scopes. The 86-variable example contains substantial redundancy and reduces to two scopes, so it does not establish scalability for difficult scope-selection problems.

Reproducibility is incomplete: the manuscript claims a public implementation without providing a repository link, and experimental kernel choices, exploration schedules, and acquisition-optimisation settings are insufficiently specified. Benchmark equations also contain consequential inconsistencies: Appendix A.1.2 omits Cancer from the PSA equation but adds it in the subsequent derivation, while Appendix A.3 defines C4 using itself. These must be corrected to verify the reported optima and regret calculations.
